findings.text: Clicking a column header no longer sorts the grid. `sort_rows: rows => rows` (SessionTasksGrid.js, the `new DataGrid` options) replaces DataGrid's own `sort_rows` (ext/DataGrid/DataGrid.js:267), which is the only code that sorts, so the comment "a header click still re-sorts" is false. DataGrid's default already returns the rows untouched when no sort is set, so the simple fix is to delete that line.

The new CSS prefix `stg-` (SessionTasksGrid.css) is not registered in `public/framework/styles/css-scopes.txt`. `stl-` is there (line 272) and `stg` is not. The new-css-class rule (/framework/code/css/doc/rules.md#5) requires the entry.

The tab shows its count twice: "135 tasks" in the grid's own head row and "135 rows" in DataGrid's bar below it, with a tall gap between the two rows (after-1920.png and after-390.png, the band above the table). One count is enough, either by hiding `.stg .datagrid-count` or by dropping `$count`. The Table/Rail toggle also appears, but the brief asked for one table, and Rail was never shown working.

At 390 the Day cell wraps to "2026- / 10-25" and Kind wraps to "agent / task" (after-390.png, table band). Both rows double in height. Wider columns, or `white-space: nowrap` on those two cells, would keep each row to one line, and the box already scrolls sideways.

after-1920.png ends at the table header, so no grid row appears at desktop width. The row check rests on after-390.png, after-day.png and the numbers in proof-out.json (135 = 135 = 21+34+28+19+2+31, scrollWidth 390, 0 page errors). Those numbers do meet the proof the brief asked for.

"Live" works only as far as SessionWork itself is live. `on_paint` fires on load and when an approval changes (SessionWork.js:49), and the tree from ai/index.json is read once. A task created after the page opens appears in neither view until a reload. That matches the brief ("the same feed SessionWork gets"), but it is worth knowing.
